newsitem.title: UK: UK urges European law change after EU work ruling.
newsitem.headline: UK urges European law change after EU work ruling.

text.p: Britain said on Tuesday it will require changes in European law after a legal decision rejecting a challenge to a directive on working hours.

A spokeswoman for Prime Minister John Major's office said Britain would block any new agreements on European Union reform as part of an Intergovernmental Conference now under way unless those treaty changes were made.
The spokeswoman said details of the ruling were only just coming in, and they would be studying it closely before further comment.

Britain argues that the EU law -- which sets an average maximum work week of 48 hours -- should be thrown out. It argues the law was improperly adopted under health rules, which require support of only a majority of EU countries instead of under EU rules requiring unanimity.

Union leader John Monks of Britain's Trade Union Congress (TUC) welcomed the decision, saying: "I think this is very good news for British workers...this is a major contribution by the European Union."

The Conservatives, trailing in polls with just six months at most to a general election, are split on Europe. The ruling will increase pressure on Major from party members enraged at what they see as Europe's encroachment on British sovereignty.
